To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
children with autism have a profile of deficits that is far from universal and that the profile is dynamic over time.
Children with autism showed poor ToM, EF and CC at both time points, but the profile was not universal.
Children with autism have a range of cognitive deficits at intake, but these deficits are not universal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature and origins of cognitive deficits in autism.
the development of cognitive skills in individuals with autism.
understanding how children with autism acquire the cognitive skills they need to function in the world, and to develop a more complete account of how autism is manifested.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the autistic mind is a mind that is not normal, but it is a mind that can be normal in some respects, at some time points, for some individuals, and in some ways.
there is no evidence that the core cognitive deficits of autism are stable across the first 3 years of life.
there is no evidence that the deficits in autism are multiple and that they develop in the same way in all autistic children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the children with autism were impaired in their ToM and EF skills compared to their peers, but that the profile was far less uniform than previously reported and that there was considerable change in ToM and some change in EF skills over the 3 year period.
there is no single core deficit in autism and that the profile of strengths and weaknesses is highly variable.
the core cognitive skills of autism do not appear to be static.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cognitive profiles of autistic individuals can change over time.
there is no one single profile of cognitive strengths and weaknesses in autism.
the profile of cognitive deficits in autism is highly variable and dynamic.
